remarks.name: Thibault Sottiaux
remarks.role: Codex & ChatGPT OpenAI
remarks.text:
We've investigated a few messages about codex usage limits being different. That's not something we change without engaging the community and being transparent.

What we did see is that when talking to affected users many were using sub2api. Converting a subscription into api traffic to then re-serve or share across many users is not something we support and this type of usage gets flagged by our fraud-prevention systems.

You are completely fine if you use your subscription through Sign in With ChatGPT, either through the official clients or through one of the many OSS clients (Pi, OpenCode, ...) that support signing in with your account and using your included usage.
remarks.translation: 我们调查了一些关于codex使用限制存在差异的消息。这不是我们会在不与社区沟通并保持透明的情况下更改的内容。我们确实看到的是，在与受影响的用户沟通时，许多人正在使用sub2api。将订阅转换为API流量，然后再重新服务或分享给众多用户，这不是我们支持的做法，这类使用方式会被我们的防欺诈系统标记。如果你通过“使用ChatGPT登录”来使用你的订阅，无论是通过官方客户端，还是通过众多支持使用你的账户登录并使用你包含用量的开源客户端（Pi、OpenCode等），都完全没有问题。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
Great post on what post training looks like for applied AI use-cases to bring down costs and improve accuracy on certain tasks. This will increasingly be an approach that companies that can get closer to the underlying workflow in an enterprise will take.

The key is that once you understand a domain well enough and have enough volume on a set of similar tasks, it can start to make sense to purpose design models just for that work.

“In post-training, we incentivized efficient tool use and reasoning through reward shaping, preferring trajectories that would reduce tokens consumed at inference-time given equivalent performance. This allowed us to co-optimize for both cost and quality, gaining significant performance while keeping cost stable.”

Now, this won’t make sense in every domain, as general purpose frontier closed or open models will be good enough out of the box -or necessary- for the work at hand. But once you have deep enough vertical expertise, and either the costs are too high to do at scale *or* you have a unique enough task type not being trained on otherwise, this will make a ton of sense. 

Very compelling value proposition for being an applied AI company, and awesome to see multiple paths to winning in the market right now.
remarks.translation: 关于应用型AI用例的后训练如何降低成本并提升特定任务准确性的精彩文章。对于能够更深入企业底层工作流的公司来说，这将日益成为一种可取的路径。关键在于，一旦你对某个领域理解得足够深入，并且在一组相似任务上拥有足够的规模，专门为这类工作设计模型就开始变得有意义了。“在后训练中，我们通过奖励塑造来激励高效的工具使用和推理能力，在同等性能下优先选择能在推理时减少token消耗的轨迹。这让我们能够同时优化成本与质量，在保持成本稳定的同时获得显著性能提升。”当然，这并非在每个领域都合理，因为通用前沿闭源或开源模型开箱即用就足够好——或者对当前工作而言是必需的。但一旦你拥有足够深厚的垂直专业知识，并且要么规模化成本过高，要么你的任务类型足够独特、没有其他模型在训练，这种做法就会非常有意义。作为一家应用型AI公司，这是极具吸引力的价值主张，也很高兴看到当前市场上有多种制胜路径。

remarks.name: Madhu Guru
remarks.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
remarks.text:
How to build great evals - part 4

The reason enterprises struggle with building decent AI systems is the lack of an eval strategy.

You need a laddered eval strategy, for your unique use cases,
with multiple evals on the cost/realism spectrum.

Here are the key kinds of evals you need:

Hill-climb long evals : this pushes the frontier of your product and you need to continually refresh this to improve quality and expand your feature base.

Regression evals : Did we break the product of today while hill climbing?

Smoke test evals: safety and the absolute basics that just can’t go wrong. Not necessarily hard questions, but important to not get wrong. Eg product identity.

Launch evals: often close to an online test with real-ish traffic. Less control, but the most realistic.

More in tomorrow’s post! 

Share with your teammates who will benefit!
remarks.translation: 如何构建出色的评估——第4部分 企业之所以难以构建像样的AI系统，是因为缺乏评估策略。你需要针对自己独特的用例，制定一套阶梯式评估策略，在成本/真实性的光谱上设置多重评估。以下是你需要的关键评估类型： 爬坡长评估：这推动你产品的前沿，你需要不断刷新它，以提升质量并扩展功能基础。 回归评估：我们在爬坡时是否破坏了今天的产品？ 冒烟测试评估：安全性和绝对不能出错的最基本事项。不一定是难题，但绝不能出错。例如产品身份。 上线评估：通常接近带有真实流量的在线测试。控制较少，但最真实。 更多内容见明天的帖子！ 分享给你的团队成员，他们会受益！

remarks.name: Peter Yang
remarks.role: Practical AI tutorials and interviews for busy people
remarks.text:
My gut is that alot of AI output can be improved just by building a loop where a manager agent negs the other worker agent with prompts like:

"Are you sure this is the best you can do?"
"I think you can do better, try again"
"Take a closer look, give me 11/10 output"
remarks.translation: 我的直觉是，很多AI输出其实可以通过构建一个循环来改进，在这个循环中，一个管理者代理用诸如“你确定这是你最好的表现吗？”“我觉得你能做得更好，再试一次”“再仔细看看，给我11/10的输出”这样的提示来贬低其他工作代理。

podcasts.title: 微软对为智能体而生的互联网的愿景——与首席技术官凯文·斯科特对话（播客精选）
podcasts.originalTitle: Microsoft’s Vision for an Internet Made for Agents With CTO Kevin Scott (Best of the Pod)
podcasts.excerpt: 2025年，凯文·斯科特押注智能体网络将成为人工智能领域的下一件大事。这位微软首席技术官认为，要让智能体真正有用，它们需要能够代表我们采取行动——这意味着要让它们访问构成互联网的同样庞杂的工具、数据和系统。如今，这一押注开始见效，因为智能体网络的基础设施正在建设中。在本周的AI & I节目中，丹·希珀重温了他与凯文的对话。他们讨论了微软在智能体网络中的角色、为什么开放性不必以牺牲安全性为代价，以及为什么程序员应该对新工具保持好奇，而不是出于原则而抵制它们。如果你觉得本期节目有趣，请点赞、订阅、评论并分享！想听到更多丹·希珀的内容：订阅Every：https://…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: In 2025, Kevin Scott bet that the agentic web would be the next big thing in AI.The Microsoft CTO argued that for agents to be genuinely useful, they'd need to be able to take action on our behalf—which would mean giving them access to the same sprawl of tools, data, and systems that make up the internet. Today, that bet is starting to pay off, as the foundational infrastructure for the agentic web is now being built.On this week's AI & I, Dan Shipper revisits his conversation with Kevin. They discuss Microsoft's role in the agentic web, why openness doesn't have to come at the expense of security, and why programmers should stay curious about new tools rather than resist them on principle.If you found this episode interesting, please like, subscribe, comment, and share!To hear more from Dan Shipper:Subscribe to Every: https://…
